gp.heading: Gross profit
gp.text: Gross profit as a percentage of revenue was 65.0% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 70.5% for the prior-year period, and 66.7% for the first nine months of 2026, compared to 69.0% for the prior-year period. The decrease in gross profit for the third quarter is primarily from the increase in Rhyz manufacturing revenue in proportion to the core Nu Skin business, which has a lower gross margin. In addition, our Rhyz manufacturing gross margin decreased for the third quarter from product mix and revenue mix among the manufacturing entities. Gross profit as a percentage of revenue for our Nu Skin business decreased 1.1 percentage points to 76.6% for the third quarter of 2026 and decreased 0.2 percentage points to 77.1% for the first nine months of 2026. The third quarter gross profit decline for the Nu Skin business was primarily attributable to higher inventory write-offs in the period.

opex.text: Historically, our principal uses of cash have included operating expenses (particularly selling expenses) and working capital (principally inventory purchases), as well as capital expenditures, stock repurchases, dividends, and debt repayment. We have at times incurred long-term debt, or drawn on our revolving line of credit, to fund strategic transactions, stock repurchases, capital investments and short-term operating needs. Historically, we have typically generated positive cash flow from operations due to favorable margins and have generally relied on cash from operations to fund operating activities; however, our operating activities used cash in the first nine months of 2026, as described below. In the first nine months of 2026, we had a net outflow of $1.4 million in cash from operations, compared to $63.7 million of cash provided by operations in the prior-year period. The decrease in cash flow from operations primarily reflects incremental inventory purchases, lower collections of accounts receivable, and higher payments of accrued expenses.

The decrease in cash flow from operations primarily reflects incremental inventory purchases, lower collections of accounts receivable, and higher payments of accrued expenses.

ga.heading: General and administrative expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses decreased to $93.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $104.8 million in the prior-year period, and decreased to $283.3 million in the first nine months of 2026, compared to $324.7 million in the prior-year period. The $10.9 million decline for the third quarter is primarily from an $8.0 million contraction in labor expenses primarily from lower incentive compensation from a decline in performance and a $4.0 million decline in software and related contracts from continued cost management, partially offset by a $5.1 million increase in cash severance expense in the period associated with recent cost saving efforts. The $41.5 million decline for the first nine months of 2026 is primarily from a $22.3 million reduction in labor expense and an $11.8 million decline in software and related contracts, partially offset by a $6.7 million increase in cash severance expense in the period associated with recent cost saving efforts. General and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenue increased to 30.2% for the third quarter of 2026, from 28.8% for the prior-year period, and increased to 29.8% for the first nine months of 2026, from 29.1% for the prior-year period.

nonop.heading: Interest expense
nonop.text: Interest expense decreased to $3.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $4.1 million in the prior-year period. Interest expense for the first nine months of 2026 increased to $11.1 million compared to $10.0 million for the prior-year period. The increase for the first nine months of 2026 is primarily due to the maturity on July 31, 2025 of our interest rate swap arrangements, which increased our effective interest rate, partially offset by lower average outstanding borrowings. The decrease for the third quarter of 2026 is primarily due to lower average outstanding borrowings, which were $216.7 million compared to $250.0 million in the prior-year period, and lower variable interest rates.

tax.heading: Provision for income taxes
tax.text: Provision (benefit) for income taxes for the three- and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026 was $2.6 million and $190.0 million, respectively, compared to $(1.1) million and $32.3 million for the prior-year periods. The effective tax rates for the three- and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026 were 139.3% and (323.8)% of pre-tax income, respectively, compared to (6.8)% and 18.1% in the prior-year periods. The change in the effective tax rate in the third quarter of 2026 is primarily due to a U.S. consolidated book loss and its impact on the annualized effective tax rate. The change in the effective tax rate in the first nine months of 2026 is primarily due to the valuation allowance established on our U.S. deferred tax assets.

net.heading: Net income (loss)
net.text: As a result of the foregoing factors, net income (loss) for the third quarter of 2026 was $(0.7) million compared to $17.1 million in the prior-year period. Net income (loss) for the first nine months of 2026 was $(248.7) million, compared to $145.7 million for the first nine months of 2025.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: Revenue for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026 decreased 14.6% to $311.0 million, compared to $364.2 million in the prior-year period. Revenue for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026 decreased 14.6% to $951.7 million compared to $1,114.8 million in the prior-year period. Our revenue in the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 was negatively impacted by 1.1% and 0.3%, respectively, from foreign-currency fluctuations. For a discussion and analysis of these decreases in revenue, see “Overview” and “Segment Results,” above.

intro.text: Nu Skin Enterprises Inc. (NYSE: NUS) is an intelligent beauty and wellness company, powered by a dynamic affiliate opportunity platform, which operates in nearly 50 markets worldwide. Backed by more than 40 years of scientific research, the company’s products help people look, feel and live their best with our newly introduced Prysm iO intelligent wellness platform, an award-winning line of beauty device systems and trusted brands in personal care and wellness products. Rhyz is the strategic investment arm of Nu Skin Enterprises, formed in 2018 consisting of synergistic consumer, technology and manufacturing companies focused on innovation within the beauty, wellness and lifestyle categories.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

We rely on our sales employees, independent direct sellers and independent marketers to attract new consumers, promote repeat purchases, and educate our sales force about our products, culture and policies through training meetings.

Our ability to improve our financial performance largely depends on our ability to anticipate and react in a timely and effective manner to changes in consumer spending patterns and preferences regarding products, platforms, and business opportunities in the affiliate gig and sharing economy, including changes in how consumers discover, evaluate and purchase products.
We rely on Free Trade Agreements where available, but these agreements may be modified, suspended, or terminated, which could further increase our costs or otherwise harm our business.
Our products are primarily marketed by our sales force, and we depend on them to generate virtually all of our revenue.

We depend on our key personnel and Sales Leaders, and the loss of the services provided by any of our executive officers, other key employees or key Sales Leaders could harm our business and results of operations.
The success of our business also depends on our key Sales Leaders.
We rely on these Sales Leaders (or other sales force members that they train, collaborate with, support and service) for a substantial majority of our revenue.
We obtain some products and ingredients from sole suppliers that own or control the product formulations, ingredients or other intellectual property rights associated with such products.
Our business operations across global markets depend on a variety of interconnected technology systems, including websites, mobile applications, cloud services, data centers, databases, and networks.

Our cosmetics and conventional foods, as well as some of our dietary supplements, are not generally subject to pre-market approval or registration processes so we cannot rely upon a government safety panel to qualify or approve our products for use, and some ingredients may not have long histories of human consumption or use.

We rely upon published and unpublished safety information including clinical studies on ingredients used in our products and conduct our own clinical and safety studies on some key ingredients and products, but not all products.

We rely upon patent, copyright, trademark, and trade secret laws in the United States and other markets, and non-disclosure, confidentiality, and other types of agreements with our employees, sales force , customers, suppliers and other parties, to establish, maintain and enforce our intellectual property rights.

Moreover, many of our products rely on technologies developed or licensed by third parties, and we may not be able to obtain or continue to obtain licenses and technologies from these third parties on reasonable terms or at all.
In addition to patented technology, we rely on our unpatented proprietary technology, trade secrets, processes and know-how.
